limitations_and_boundaries: Geneformer's predictions are based solely on transcriptional data and may not capture post-transcriptional or epigenetic regulatory mechanisms.
In silico deletion is a computational approximation and may not fully recapitulate biological gene knockout effects.
Experimental validation was limited to a subset of predicted targets (GSN, PLN) in a specific disease model (TTN truncating mutation).
Fine-tuning hyperparameters were not individually optimized per task, potentially underestimating maximum predictive potential.
Pretraining corpus Genecorpus-30M is limited to human data; applicability to other species is not tested.
The selected source chunks do not report a rescue, reconstitution, reversal, or epistasis experiment; that rung of the causal evidence chain remains untested within this extraction scope.

research_questions.statement: Can transfer learning with a deep learning model pretrained on large-scale single-cell transcriptomic data enable context-specific predictions in network biology with limited data?

provenance.text_excerpt: Geneformer predicted candidate therapeutic targets whose experimental targeting in an iPSC disease model led to significant functional improvement.

claims.statement: Geneformer can identify candidate therapeutic targets for cardiomyopathy via in silico treatment analysis, with experimental validation for GSN and PLN.

datasets.description: Single-nucleus profiling of human dilated and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (ref. 35). Training: non-failing n=9, hypertrophic n=11, dilated n=9, total 93,589 cells. Out-of-sample: non-failing n=4, hypertrophic n=4, dilated n=2, total 39,006 cells.
datasets.name: Cardiomyocyte dataset for fine-tuning

experiments_or_tasks: Experimental validation: CRISPR-mediated knockout of Geneformer-predicted targets GSN and PLN in TTN+/- iPSC-derived cardiac microtissues significantly improved contractile stress (P<0.05 Wilcoxon, FDR-corrected).

Fine-tuned Geneformer to distinguish cardiomyocytes from non-failing hearts (n=9), hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (n=11), and dilated cardiomyopathy (n=9). Out-of-sample accuracy 90% (precision 82%, recall 87%) on 39,006 cells.
In silico deletion or activation of genes in non-failing cardiomyocytes identified 447 genes shifting towards hypertrophic state and 478 towards dilated state.
In silico treatment analysis in disease cardiomyocytes identified candidate therapeutic targets. Top pathways for hypertrophic included ADCY5 and SRPK3.

methods.name: Fine-tuning for cardiomyopathy classification and in silico treatment
methods.protocol_description: Fine-tuned Geneformer to classify cardiomyocyte phenotype (non-failing, hypertrophic, dilated) using cell-level labels. In silico deletion/activation: remove or add a gene's rank value encoding and measure shift in cell embedding towards disease states. In silico treatment: in disease cells, delete or activate genes and measure shift towards non-failing state. Experimental validation: CRISPR-mediated knockout in iPSC-derived cardiac microtissues with TTN truncating mutation.

provenance.text_excerpt: CRISPR-mediated knockout of both Geneformer-predicted targets GSN and PLN in the TTN+/− cells significantly improved the contractile stress of the TTN+/− cardiac microtissues, validating these genes as promising candidate therapeutic targets for this disease (Fig. 6f,g and Extended Data Fig. 10e).

results.value_raw_text: CRISPR-mediated knockout of both Geneformer-predicted targets GSN and PLN in the TTN+/− cells significantly improved the contractile stress of the TTN+/− cardiac microtissues (P<0.05 Wilcoxon, FDR-corrected)

claims.statement: In silico deletion using Geneformer can model gene network connections and cooperative action of transcription factors.

experiments_or_tasks: In silico deletion of TBX5 similarly impacted direct targets more than indirect and housekeeping genes.
Performed in silico deletion of GATA4 in fetal cardiomyocytes and measured effect on gene embeddings. Direct GATA4 targets (by ChIP-seq) were significantly more impacted than indirect targets.
Tested combinatorial in silico deletion of GATA4 and TBX5. Combination had greater impact on cobound targets than sum of individual deletions, suggesting cooperative action.

methods.name: In silico deletion approach
methods.protocol_description: In silico deletion of a gene is performed by removing that gene from the input rank value encoding and evaluating the change in contextual gene embeddings (cosine similarity). A more deleterious effect corresponds to lower cosine similarity to the original embedding.

study_units.name: In silico deletion reveals network connections

provenance.text_excerpt: direct GATA4 targets (as defined by ChIP–seq33) were significantly more impacted by in silico deletion of GATA4 in fetal cardiomyocytes compared to indirect targets (Fig. 5a).

results.value_raw_text: In silico deletion of GATA4 was significantly more deleterious to GATA4 direct targets than to housekeeping genes, NOTCH1 targets, NKX2-5 targets, or indirect targets (P<0.05 Wilcoxon, FDR-corrected)

datasets.description: Large-scale pretraining corpus comprising 29.9 million human single-cell transcriptomes from a broad range of tissues.
datasets.name: Genecorpus-30M

experiments_or_tasks: Assembled Genecorpus-30M, comprising 29.9 million human single-cell transcriptomes from a broad range of tissues from publicly available data.

Geneformer architecture: six layers of transformer encoder units, input size 2048, 256 embedding dimensions, four attention heads per layer, feed-forward size 512, full dense self-attention, ReLU activation, dropout 0.02, initialization standard deviation 0.02, epsilon for layer normalization 1e-12. Implemented in PyTorch and Huggingface Transformers library.

Pretrained Geneformer on Genecorpus-30M using a self-supervised masked learning objective: 15% of genes within each transcriptome were masked and the model was trained to predict the masked gene using context of remaining unmasked genes.

Pretraining hyperparameters: max learning rate 1e-3, linear scheduler with warmup, Adam with weight decay fix, warmup steps 10,000, weight decay 0.001, batch size 12, three epochs. Efficiency measures: dynamic length-grouped padding (29.4x speedup), Deepspeed distributed GPU training across three nodes with four Nvidia V100 32GB GPUs each (total 12 GPUs), pretraining completed in approximately 3 days.

methods.name: Geneformer architecture and pretraining
methods.protocol_description: Geneformer is a context-aware, attention-based deep learning model pretrained on large-scale transcriptomic data using a self-supervised masked learning objective. Architecture includes six transformer encoder layers, input size 2048, 256 embedding dimensions, four attention heads, feed-forward size 512. Pretraining masked 15% of genes and predicted masked gene identity. Optimization used Adam with weight decay fix, learning rate 1e-3, batch size 12, three epochs. Efficiency optimized via dynamic length-grouped padding and Deepspeed distributed training.

For bivalency classification, trained on 56 conserved loci and then tested genome-wide. For regulatory range, trained on single-cell transcriptomes without ChIP-seq data.
